## CANDIDA ALBICANS
Avoid using fluconazole empirically to treat candidal infections in patients who
have received an imidazole in the previous year.
## Treatment of thrush or oropharyngeal candidiasis
Oropharyngeal candidal disease may present in different patterns, like white
plaques in the oropharyngeal area, erythematous macules (often in patients with
dentures), or as pseudomembranes. Thrush infection often recurs, especially in
patients with AIDS. Consult MRTC clinic or Infectious Diseases (MRTC may also be
consulted in the MVAHCS) for more information on treatment of recurrent
infection. Mild disease:
#Inpatient Nystatin swish and swallow q6h for 7-14 days [M]
< OR >
Clotrimazole troche 10 mg PO 5X/day for 7-14 days [M]
Moderate to severe disease:
Fluconazole 200 mg PO q24h for 7-14 days [R,DI]
## Esophageal candidiasis
Esophageal infection requires systemic therapy.
Preferred:
Fluconazole 400 mg PO q24h for 14-21 days [R,DI]
Alternative for patient who cannot swallow tablets:
Fluconazole 400 IV q24h for 14-21 days [R,DI]
<OR>
Micafungin 100-150mg IV q24h for 14-21 days
## Systemic candidal infection
Fluconazole is preferred empirical therapy in most cases. Amphotericin B should
be used empirically in patients who have received an azole antifungal drug
recently, or in patients who are critically ill.
Duration of Therapy: Duration of therapy is dependent upon location, severity of
infection, and response to therapy. Consult Infectious Diseases for more
information.
Preferred:
Fluconazole 800 mg PO once then 400 mg PO q24h [R,DI]
< OR >
Fluconazole 800 mg IV once then 400 mg IV q24h [R,DI]
Recent azole antifungal treatment:
Liposomal amphotericin (Ambisome) 3-5 mg/kg IV q24h [R,O]
< OR >
Micafungin 100-150 mg IV q24h [H,DI]
